nodes.description: Osteosarcoma genomes carry some of the highest structural variant burdens of any pediatric cancer, and these rearrangements recur at a small number of genomic hotspots. In a 236-genome whole-genome sequencing series (preprint, not yet peer reviewed), five hotspots of clustered structural variation were altered in 58% of tumors; four were associated with amplification of the oncogenes MYC, CCND3, CCNE1 and CDK4, and the fifth mapped largely upstream of TP53. Single cells carrying hotspot events converged on a less differentiated, neural crest-like transcriptional program, and the events were detectable in liquid biopsies. Earlier peer-reviewed whole-genome sequencing had already identified MYC and CCNE1 among the recurrently altered loci.

nodes.description: Osteosarcoma is characterized by extreme genomic disorganization including aneuploidy, chromosomal amplifications, deletions, and complex rearrangements. Unlike many other sarcomas, osteosarcoma lacks conserved translocations or recurrent fusion genes, instead exhibiting heterogeneous somatic copy number alterations.

evidence.reference_title: Deciphering the Signaling Mechanisms of Osteosarcoma Tumorigenesis.
evidence.snippet: In contrast to many other sarcomas, OS lacks conserved translocations or genetic mutations; instead, it has heterogeneous abnormalities, including somatic DNA copy number alteration, ploidy, chromosomal amplification, and chromosomal loss and gain.

evidence.reference_title: Biology and pathogenesis of human osteosarcoma.
evidence.snippet: Its most common feature is genome disorganization, aneuploidy with chromosomal alterations, deregulation of tumor suppressor genes and of the cell cycle, and an absence of DNA repair.
Among other genes mutated in more than 10% of OS cases, c-Myc plays a role in OS development and promotes cell invasion by activating MEK-ERK pathways.

nodes.description: Amplification of MYC, one of the oncogenes recurrently altered in osteosarcoma, increases the dosage of the MYC protein, a bHLH-ZIP transcription factor that activates and represses genes involved in proliferation, energy production, metabolism and translation.
